name: DNA
hook: The double helix: what DNA is, how it copies and mutates, and what it proved.

facts.label: deoxyribonucleic acid
facts.statement: DNA stands for deoxyribonucleic acid, the molecule that carries genetic information in living cells.

facts.label: the double helix
facts.statement: In 1953 James Watson and Francis Crick built the double helix model of DNA; Watson's book about the discovery is The Double Helix.

facts.label: base pairs
facts.statement: Each rung of the DNA double helix is a base pair such as A-T, linking the two strands of the molecule.

facts.label: the human genome
facts.statement: The human genome is all 3 billion base pairs of DNA in a person; the Human Genome Project finished mapping it in 2003.

facts.label: mutation
facts.statement: A mutation is a change in the sequence of DNA bases; a single point mutation causes sickle-cell anemia.

facts.label: chromosomes
facts.statement: Chromosomes are threadlike structures of DNA and protein in the cell nucleus; humans have 46 of them.

facts.label: DNA testing
facts.statement: DNA testing has identified remains and exposed impostors: Anna Anderson was not Anastasia, and Richard III's bones were matched through living relatives.
